subject: Your account has been limited
body:
Dear Customer,

We noticed unusual activity on your PayPal account and have temporarily limited what you can do with it.

To restore full access, please verify your identity within 24 hours. If we do not hear from you, your account will be permanently suspended and any remaining balance will be held for 180 days.

Verify now: paypa1.com/account/verify-identity

Thank you for being a valued customer.
PayPal Account Services

red_flags.explanation: The sender domain is paypa1.com: the letter 'l' has been swapped for the digit '1'. Real PayPal mail comes from paypal.com.
The link goes to the look-alike domain paypa1.com, not paypal.com.
An artificial deadline with a threat of permanent suspension is designed to make you act before thinking.

subject: Receipt for your payment to Greenleaf Books
body:
Hello Jordan Ellison,

You sent a payment of $24.99 USD to Greenleaf Books.

Transaction ID: 4KD29581MX3307418
Date: October 19, 2026
Paid with: Visa ending in 7741

It may take a few moments for this transaction to appear in your account activity.

If you have questions about this purchase, contact Greenleaf Books directly. To view the details, sign in to your account the way you usually do.

PayPal
why_legit: Sent from paypal.com, greets you by name, contains specific transaction details, and asks you to sign in the usual way rather than clicking a link.

subject: Your October eStatement is ready
body:
Hi Jordan,

Your eStatement for checking account ending in 2290 is now available.

You can view it in online banking under Accounts > Statements, or in the Harbor FCU mobile app.

Reminder: Harbor FCU will never ask for your password, PIN, or one-time code by email, text, or phone.

Thanks for banking with us,
Harbor Federal Credit Union
Member Services: 1-800-555-0142
why_legit: No link to click, no request for credentials, uses your name and a partial account number, and points you to the app or website you already use.

subject: Warning: Your Windows licence has expired
body:
Microsoft Windows Defender has detected that your licence key has expired and 3 viruses were found on your computer.

Your personal files and banking details are at risk. Call our certified technicians IMMEDIATELY on +1 (888) 555-0199 or download the repair tool below.

Download repair tool: micros0ft-support.com/repair/WinFix.exe

Failure to act will result in your computer being locked.

Microsoft Technical Department

red_flags.explanation: 'micros0ft' uses a zero instead of the letter 'o'. Microsoft does not send unsolicited virus warnings from a support domain.
The link downloads an executable (.exe) from the fake domain, a classic way to deliver malware.
Tech-support scams push you to phone them so a 'technician' can take remote control of your computer.

subject: Security alert: someone has your password
body:
Someone just used your password to try to sign in to your Google Account from Lagos, Nigeria.

Google stopped this sign-in attempt, but you must confirm your identity now or your account will be deleted.

Confirm your password here: g00gle.com/accounts/confirm-password

The Google Accounts team

red_flags.explanation: Replies go to g00gle-verify.net, a different domain from the sender. Legitimate account alerts do not route replies elsewhere.
'g00gle' uses two zeros. Google never asks you to 'confirm your password' via an email link.
Threatening to delete your account is a pressure tactic; real security alerts let you review activity calmly.

subject: Security alert: new sign-in on Windows
body:
New sign-in to your account

jordan.ellison.dev@gmail.com

We noticed a new sign-in to your Google Account on a Windows device. If this was you, you don't need to do anything. If not, we'll help you secure your account.

Check activity in your Google Account at myaccount.google.com/notifications

You received this email to let you know about important changes to your Google Account and services.
why_legit: Comes from accounts.google.com, no threats or deadlines, says 'if this was you, you don't need to do anything', and the link points to the genuine google.com domain.

subject: Quick favour — need this done today
body:
Hi,

Are you at your desk? I'm in back-to-back meetings with investors and can't take calls.

I need you to buy 8 Apple gift cards at $200 each for a client appreciation surprise. Keep this confidential — I don't want it to spoil the surprise. Scratch the backs and email me photos of the codes as soon as possible.

I'll make sure you're reimbursed by end of day.

Margaret
Sent from my iPhone

red_flags.explanation: The reply-to is a personal Gmail address, not the company domain. Your answer would go straight to the attacker.
The company domain is brightpath-consulting.com, but this one ends in '.co', a look-alike registered by the attacker.
Secrecy plus gift cards is the hallmark of CEO fraud. Always verify money requests by phone or in person.

subject: Notes from Tuesday's sprint planning
body:
Hi team,

Thanks for a productive session on Tuesday. Quick recap:

- Dashboard redesign moves to sprint 14 (owner: Marcus)
- API rate-limit bug is top priority this week (owner: Jordan)
- Retro moved to Friday 3pm because of the all-hands

The full notes are in the shared Projects folder under Sprint 13. Shout if I missed anything.

Cheers,
Priya
why_legit: From a colleague on the real company domain, references real shared context, no links, no requests for money or credentials.

subject: Benefits open enrolment closes 15 November
body:
Hello everyone,

A reminder that open enrolment for 2027 health and dental benefits runs until 15 November.

If you're happy with your current plan, you don't need to do anything — it will roll over automatically.

To make changes, open the HR portal from the intranet home page and choose Benefits > 2027 Enrolment. Drop-in Q&A sessions are on Thursdays at 12:30 in the Atrium.

Best,
The People Team
why_legit: Internal sender, a reasonable deadline weeks away, explains that doing nothing is fine, and directs you to the intranet rather than an emailed link.

subject: Problem with your order #112-4471902-883
body:
Hello,

We were unable to process payment for your recent order (Apple AirPods Pro, $249.00). Your order will be cancelled and your account suspended unless you update your billing information.

Update payment details: arnazon.com/your-account/billing-update

We apologise for the inconvenience.
Amazon Customer Service

red_flags.explanation: 'arnazon' uses 'r' + 'n' to imitate the letter 'm'. At a glance it reads as 'amazon'.
The billing link points to the look-alike domain. Always open your account directly instead of using email links.
Threatening suspension over an order you may not have placed is meant to trigger panic.

subject: We missed you: parcel waiting — small fee required
body:
Your parcel could not be delivered today because the customs fee of $1.99 was unpaid.

To schedule redelivery, pay the outstanding fee within 48 hours, otherwise the item will be returned to sender.

Pay fee and book redelivery: parcel-redelivery-fee.com/pay?ref=PX99031

Parcel Delivery Service

red_flags.explanation: A tiny 'fee' is bait to capture your full card details. Real couriers are named and use their own domain.
A deadline with the threat of returning your parcel pushes you to pay without checking.

subject: Your Amazon.com order of "USB-C Hub, 7-in-1" has shipped
body:
Hello Jordan,

Good news — your package is on its way.

Order #113-8820461-5529117
USB-C Hub, 7-in-1
Arriving: Thursday, October 23

Track your package from Your Orders on amazon.com or in the Amazon app.

We hope to see you again soon.
Amazon.com
why_legit: Sent from amazon.com, uses your name, matches a specific order with a delivery date, and only asks you to check Your Orders in the usual place.

subject: Copyright infringement notice on your account
body:
Your account has been reported for copyright infringement on a recent post.

If you believe this is a mistake, you must submit an appeal form. If you don't, your account will be permanently deleted in 24 hours.

Submit appeal: lnstagram.com/appeal-form/login

Instagram Copyright Team

red_flags.explanation: The domain starts with a lowercase 'L', not a capital 'I'. In many fonts 'lnstagram' and 'Instagram' look identical.
Replies go to insta-copyright-review.net, a different domain from the sender.
Fake copyright notices use extreme deadlines to rush you into entering your login on the 'appeal form'.

subject: Daniel Okafor wants to connect
body:
Hi Jordan,

Daniel Okafor, Senior Data Engineer at Northwind Analytics, would like to join your professional network.

You have 4 mutual connections, including Priya Raman.

You can accept or ignore this invitation from My Network in the LinkedIn app or on linkedin.com.

You are receiving invitation emails. Unsubscribe in your settings.
why_legit: Genuine linkedin.com sender, no urgency, nothing to pay or log in to via the email, and mutual connections you recognise.

subject: BBQ at ours on Saturday?
body:
Hey!

We're doing a BBQ at ours this Saturday from about 2pm, weather permitting. Bring whoever you like — Alex is doing his famous veggie burgers again.

Let me know if you can make it so I know how much to buy.

Sam
why_legit: A friend writing from their usual personal address, conversational tone, no links, no attachments, no requests for money or details.

subject: CONGRATULATIONS!!! You have won $850,000.00
body:
ATTENTION WINNER,

Your email address was selected in our annual International Email Lottery and you have WON the sum of $850,000.00 USD.

To claim your prize, reply with your full name, home address, date of birth, and bank account details to our claims agent Dr. Harold Benson.

You must respond within 72 hours or your winnings will be forfeited.

Yours faithfully,
International Lotto Commission

red_flags.explanation: Replies go to a personal Outlook address, not the 'commission' that supposedly sent it.

red_flags.match: reply with your full name, home address, date of birth, and bank account details
red_flags.explanation: No genuine lottery asks for bank details by email, and you cannot win a lottery you never entered.

red_flags.match: within 72 hours or your winnings will be forfeited
red_flags.explanation: A deadline stops you from asking anyone whether it is real.

subject: Your email won the Microsoft 2026 anniversary draw
body:
Dear Lucky Winner,

Your email was randomly chosen as one of five winners of the Microsoft 2026 Anniversary Draw. Your prize is $500,000 and a Surface Laptop.

To release your prize, a one-time processing fee of $350 must be paid by gift card or cryptocurrency.

Claim here: micros0ft-support.com/rewards/claim-prize

Microsoft Promotions Department

red_flags.explanation: The same zero-for-'o' look-alike domain used in the fake tech-support email.

red_flags.match: processing fee of $350 must be paid by gift card or cryptocurrency
red_flags.explanation: Advance-fee fraud: a real prize never requires you to pay first, and gift cards or crypto are untraceable.
The claim link points to the look-alike domain.

subject: Charity raffle results — thank you!
body:
Hi all,

Thanks to everyone who bought tickets for last week's charity raffle — together we raised $1,240 for the Riverside Food Bank!

Winning tickets:
1st prize (weekend break): ticket 0417
2nd prize (coffee machine): ticket 0093
3rd prize (cinema vouchers): ticket 0262

If you hold a winning ticket, pop by the reception desk with it any time this week to collect your prize.

The Social Committee
why_legit: A raffle you actually entered, from the internal company domain, asks for nothing except collecting the prize in person.
